articles.title: Newegg Secures $100 Million Senior Credit Facility Led By East West Bank
articles.snippet:
Newegg Commerce has closed a $100 million senior credit facility led and arranged by East West Bank, giving the technology e-commerce company additional financial flexibility as it continues investing in growth initiatives.
The post Newegg Secures $100 Million Senior Credit Facility Led By East West Bank appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Newegg Secures $100 Million Senior Credit Facility Led By East West Bank
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 21, 2026
Newegg Secures $100 Million Senior Credit Facility Led By East West Bank
Newegg Commerce has closed a $100 million senior credit facility led and arranged by East West Bank, giving the technology e-commerce company additional financial flexibility as it continues investing in growth initiatives.
The facility includes participation from a syndicate of lenders and replaces Newegg’s previous credit arrangements, which matured in August 2026.
Newegg said the expanded financing strengthens its financial position and provides additional flexibility as the company manages ongoing supply dynamics and continues investing across its business.
The transaction also extends the longstanding relationship between Newegg and East West Bank. The lending group cited Newegg’s business model, operating performance, and future growth opportunities as factors supporting the financing.
Newegg plans to continue directing resources toward e-commerce innovation, AI-enabled capabilities, and deeper partnerships with technology brands, suppliers, and customers worldwide.
The company operates an e-commerce platform serving technology enthusiasts, businesses, gamers, PC builders, and IT professionals. Its product portfolio includes PC hardware, consumer electronics, gaming peripherals, servers, workstations, and AI infrastructure.
Newegg also provides services for independent sellers, including marketing, supply chain, and technical solutions intended to help third-party businesses expand through its platform.
The new credit facility gives Newegg additional borrowing capacity as it invests in those areas and navigates changing conditions across the technology supply chain.
Founded in 2001 and headquartered in Diamond Bar, California, Newegg Commerce is publicly traded on Nasdaq under the ticker NEGG. The company has operated for more than two decades and has expanded from its core PC hardware business into a broader technology commerce and services platform.
The $100 million facility expands Newegg’s prior credit arrangements and provides additional capital to support its strategic priorities and ongoing operations.
KEY QUOTES:
“Closing this new facility is an important step for Newegg in further strengthening our financial position and provides us with greater flexibility to navigate ongoing supply dynamics while we continue to invest in growth. We appreciate the commitment and partnership from East West Bank and the rest of our lending group, and the confidence they have shown in Newegg.”
Christina Ching, Chief Financial Officer Of Newegg
“We are pleased to provide this important debt financing to Newegg, a longstanding client in the e-commerce space. This transaction reflects the strength of our relationship, our confidence in their business model, and our commitment to delivering tailored capital solutions to leading growth companies like Newegg. We look forward to supporting their next phase of expansion.”
East West Bank statement

articles.title: Meshy Surpasses $100 Million In ARR After Raising Nearly $400 Million At $1.5 Billion Valuation
articles.snippet:
Meshy surpassed $100 million in annual recurring revenue, up approximately 100-fold from $1 million in less than two years.
The post Meshy Surpasses $100 Million In ARR After Raising Nearly $400 Million At $1.5 Billion Valuation appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Meshy Surpasses $100 Million In ARR After Raising Nearly $400 Million At $1.5 Billion Valuation
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 11, 2026
Meshy Surpasses $100 Million In ARR After Raising Nearly $400 Million At $1.5 Billion Valuation
Meshy surpassed $100 million in annual recurring revenue, up approximately 100-fold from $1 million in less than two years.
The milestone follows Meshy’s nearly $400 million Series B financing in July 2026 at a $1.5 billion valuation.
Meshy said the financing was the largest funding round to date for an AI 3D company.
The company now serves more than 15 million registered users and over 3,000 companies and educational institutions worldwide.
Users have generated more than 100 million 3D models through the platform.
Meshy said half of the world’s 10 most valuable companies by market capitalization or private valuation are customers.
Approximately 200 Fortune Global 500 companies also use the platform.
Meshy develops multimodal foundation models that generate production-ready 3D assets from text and images.
The company’s technology is used for gaming, film, education, and 3D printing.
Meshy recently released Meshy 7.1, which supports Ultra 4K geometry generation.
The company also open-sourced its alignment benchmark suite for image-to-3D generation.
Alongside the ARR milestone, Meshy launched official iOS and Android applications powered by Meshy 7.
The mobile app enables users to convert photos, sketches, and text into textured 3D models while providing printability checks, AI repair, augmented reality previews, and exports in formats including STL, GLB, FBX, OBJ, USDZ, and 3MF.
Meshy was founded by Ethan Hu, who holds a Ph.D. from MIT.
KEY QUOTES:
“Surpassing $100 million in ARR in under two years reflects the growing demand for AI-powered 3D creation.”
“From game studios and film teams to educators and home 3D printing enthusiasts, our customers are showing just how broadly this technology can be used—and how much opportunity lies ahead.”
Faye Pan, Vice President of Growth at Meshy

articles.title: Stable Invests $100 Million To Support Launch Of Alchemist Capital
articles.snippet:
Stable Asset Management is providing a $100 million seed investment to support the launch and long-term growth of Alchemist Capital, a new biotechnology investment firm founded by Andy Tran.
The post Stable Invests $100 Million To Support Launch Of Alchemist Capital appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Stable Invests $100 Million To Support Launch Of Alchemist Capital
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 10, 2026
Stable Invests $100 Million To Support Launch Of Alchemist Capital
Stable Asset Management is providing a $100 million seed investment to support the launch and long-term growth of Alchemist Capital, a new biotechnology investment firm founded by Andy Tran.
New York-based Alchemist plans to invest in biotechnology companies across public and private markets.
Its strategy combines fundamental scientific research with a proprietary AI-native research and monitoring engine intended to make biotechnology investing more systematic and scalable.
The firm is targeting companies developing first-in-class or best-in-class medicines and emerging businesses that could become multi-product biotechnology platforms.
Alchemist will focus on differentiated science, potential clinical benefits, and sustainable competitive advantages.
The firm is also targeting companies using AI, computing, and data to transform drug discovery and development, along with supporting life sciences tools and technology platforms.
Tran previously helped build biotechnology investment practices at Andreessen Horowitz and Matrix Capital.
His investment experience includes Tmunity, EQRx, Erasca, Freenome, Genesis Therapeutics, Cartography Biosciences, and Maze Therapeutics.
Tran served on Maze’s board from the company’s early stages through its 2025 IPO.
Before entering investing, he studied bioengineering and computer science at Harvard and conducted CRISPR gene-editing research under Harvard Medical School professor George Church.
Stable manages approximately $5.3 billion and has supported the development of 46 alternative asset managers.
KEY QUOTES:
“Alchemist is exactly the kind of ambitious, differentiated platform Stable was built to support. Andy brings a rare combination of scientific depth, firsthand experience building biotech investment platforms, and conviction in the opportunity ahead.”
Erik Serrano Berntsen, CEO of Stable
“We established Alchemist to combine deep scientific and medical understanding with purpose-built computational infrastructure, giving us a more comprehensive diligence process and a clearer view of how new evidence changes an investment thesis. The engine doesn’t replace the fundamental work. It supercharges it.”
“Stable has helped more founders build institutions than almost anyone in asset management. That’s why we are excited to partner from day one.”
Andy Tran, Founder of Alchemist Capital

articles.text:
Spellbook: Interview With Co-Founder And CEO Scott Stevenson About Legal AI, M&A And $100 Million ARR Growth
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 8, 2026
Spellbook: Interview With Co-Founder And CEO Scott Stevenson About Legal AI, M&A And $100 Million ARR Growth
Spellbook is the leading AI infrastructure for contract workflows that is deeply integrated into Microsoft Word and Google Docs and supports contract drafting, review, negotiation, and transactional workflows, saving teams upwards of 84% on contract reviews or a full day per week on average. The company launched the first generative AI tool for lawyers in 2022 and now serves more than 5,000 in-house teams and law firms across 80 countries. Pulse 2.0 interviewed Spellbook Co-Founder and CEO Scott Stevenson to learn more about the company’s growth, its $40 million debt financing from RBCx, acquisition strategy, legal AI market consolidation, and plans to reach $100 million in annual recurring revenue.
Scott Stevenson’s Background
Screenshot
When asked about his background, Stevenson shared:
I’m CEO and co-founder of Spellbook. The short version is that at a previous startup, half our angel round went to routine legal paperwork. Most expensive bill we’d ever seen, least value delivered.
And that experience isn’t unusual: 60% of small businesses won’t even call a lawyer because they can’t afford to. That stuck with me.
We started the company in 2018, originally called Rally, and launched the first generative AI tool for lawyers in summer 2022, a few months before ChatGPT came out.
So we’ve been at this longer than most people realize. Now we have more than 5,000 customers in 80 countries, and are beginning to gain industry recognition, including the inaugural Built in Canada Rocketship award for Canada’s fastest-growing company and my inclusion on Financial Post and Caldwell Partners International Inc.’s Canada’s Top 40 Under 40 list.
$40 Million Debt Financing
When asked what drove the decision to raise $40 million in debt financing from RBCx so soon after Spellbook’s $50 million Series B, Stevenson explained:
Growth has accelerated faster than what we expected.
We’re on track to hit $100 million ARR this year after tripling revenue in 2025, and we started seeing a real opportunity to acquire smaller competitors.
The market matured very quickly, leaving competitors with good products unable to get a real foothold in the market.
Debt was the right instrument for that since it lets us move on M&A without diluting our shareholders.
RBCx got it and moved quickly.
Deploying The New Capital
When asked how Spellbook plans to deploy the new capital, particularly around pursuing up to five acquihires over the next two years, Stevenson said:
Acquisitions are the primary focus.
The legal AI market matured really quickly, and a lot of smaller companies spun up.
We expect to do roughly five deals over two years, around $60 million in total spend, though that could shift.
We’re already looking closely at two targets right now, and once every two weeks or so we hear from a company that wants to be acquired.
We’re also hiring aggressively with plans to expand our team to 250 people by year-end, which doubles our team.

articles.title: Fortitude Announces Up To $100 Million BITMAIN Zcash Miner Commitment And Expands DCG Credit Facility To $70 Million
articles.snippet:
Fortitude Mining has entered into a letter of intent with BITMAIN providing priority allocation for next-generation Zcash mining equipment through a potential purchase commitment of up to $100 million.
The post Fortitude Announces Up To $100 Million BITMAIN Zcash Miner Commitment And Expands DCG Credit Facility To $70 Million appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Fortitude Announces Up To $100 Million BITMAIN Zcash Miner Commitment And Expands DCG Credit Facility To $70 Million
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 6, 2026
Fortitude Announces Up To $100 Million BITMAIN Zcash Miner Commitment And Expands DCG Credit Facility To $70 Million
Fortitude Mining has entered into a letter of intent with BITMAIN providing priority allocation for next-generation Zcash mining equipment through a potential purchase commitment of up to $100 million.
The commitment is indicative and non-binding and remains subject to execution of a definitive purchase agreement once BITMAIN releases final equipment specifications and pricing.
The arrangement allows Fortitude to increase the size of the contemplated purchase, subject to BITMAIN’s approval and equipment availability, or reduce it following the official launch of the new hardware.
Fortitude expects BITMAIN’s next-generation Zcash mining equipment to begin shipping during the second quarter of 2027.
The company currently operates approximately 4.7 GSol/s of Equihash hashrate and has more than 60 MW of contracted power capacity across seven locations in South Dakota, Nebraska, Texas and New York.
Fortitude has also previously ordered 9,000 BITMAIN ANTMINER Z15 Pro miners.
The latest agreement is designed to give the company early access to another generation of equipment as it seeks to increase its Zcash mining capacity.
To support the potential purchase, Fortitude also expanded its credit facility with parent company Digital Currency Group from $50 million to $70 million.
The facility now provides approximately $42.7 million of remaining borrowing capacity before a planned new draw.
The BITMAIN letter of intent requires Fortitude to make a refundable deposit equal to 20% of the contemplated commitment, or $20 million.
Fortitude plans to draw that amount under the DCG credit facility, with the funding expected to be provided in ZEC and subsequently liquidated to fund the deposit.
After the planned $20 million borrowing, Fortitude expects to have borrowed approximately $47.3 million under the facility and have approximately $22.7 million of remaining capacity.
DCG may also provide additional ZEC financing outside the upsized facility to support Fortitude’s capital requirements and growth initiatives through fiscal 2027.
Fortitude is separately progressing with its previously announced proposed business combination with HeartSciences.
If completed, that transaction is expected to make Fortitude a publicly traded company and provide additional access to the capital markets as it expands its Zcash mining and energy infrastructure platform.
KEY QUOTES:
“Fortitude’s vision is to be the largest vertically-integrated Zcash mining platform. Securing a priority supply allocation for BITMAIN’s next-generation equipment, alongside our existing operating base and previously announced Z15 Pro order, positions Fortitude to expand its fleet with industry-leading hardware as it becomes available. We believe there is a significant opportunity to invest in Zcash mining infrastructure today, and Fortitude is well positioned to lead that buildout.”
Jaime Leverton, CEO of Fortitude

articles.title: Lattis Management Secures More Than $100 Million In Second Close
articles.snippet:
Lattis Management has completed a second capital close for its flagship Lattis LP vehicle and launched infrastructure-focused Lattis Infrastructure LP, securing more than $100 million in investor commitments during the early part of the third quarter.
The post Lattis Management Secures More Than $100 Million In Second Close appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Lattis Management Secures More Than $100 Million In Second Close
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 6, 2026
Lattis Management Secures More Than $100 Million In Second Close
Lattis Management has completed a second capital close for its flagship Lattis LP vehicle and launched infrastructure-focused Lattis Infrastructure LP, securing more than $100 million in investor commitments during the early part of the third quarter.
The fundraising was anchored by a Northeastern institutional investor managing more than $25 billion in assets.
Additional commitments came from family offices and institutional investors across North America and Asia-Pacific.
Lattis provides infrastructure and commodities solutions focused on the middle-market energy sector.
The second close gives the firm additional capital to pursue a pipeline of infrastructure investment opportunities as it continues fundraising for the vehicles.
Management said the firm expects to conclude fundraising in the near term.
Alongside the fund closing, Lattis appointed Tatiana Izquierdo Head of Finance.
Izquierdo joins the firm’s New York team from The Visualize Group.
She brings more than a decade of experience involving private equity structures, evergreen investment vehicles, accounting and investor reporting.
Izquierdo previously held finance positions at Two Sigma Investments, Leeds Equity Partners and PwC.
Her appointment expands Lattis’ internal infrastructure as the firm increases capital under management and deploys investments through its flagship and infrastructure vehicles.
KEY QUOTES:
“We’re delighted with the progress we’ve made on Lattis Infrastructure LP and Lattis LP. This second close reflects the strength of the relationships we’ve built with investors and our shared conviction in the enormous opportunity in middle market infrastructure.”
Arjun Kapoor, Managing Partner and Co-Founder of Lattis
“To have the backing of such notable institutions is an incredible vote of confidence in our team. We are grateful for the trust our investors have placed in us and are on track to conclude fundraising in the near term. We look forward to putting that capital to work across a strong pipeline of opportunities.”
Casey Dwyer, Managing Partner and Co-Founder of Lattis

articles.title: Rainmaker Raises $100 Million Series B To Scale Water Production And Weather Modification
articles.snippet:
Rainmaker Technology has raised $100 million in Series B funding to expand its atmospheric research organization and reduce the cost of producing freshwater through cloud seeding.
The post Rainmaker Raises $100 Million Series B To Scale Water Production And Weather Modification appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Rainmaker Raises $100 Million Series B To Scale Water Production And Weather Modification
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 2, 2026
Rainmaker Raises $100 Million Series B To Scale Water Production And Weather Modification
Rainmaker Technology has raised $100 million in Series B funding to expand its atmospheric research organization and reduce the cost of producing freshwater through cloud seeding.
The round included investments from NOA VC, Upfront Ventures, DCVC, Lowercarbon Capital, and Dream Ventures.
El Segundo, California-based Rainmaker develops weather modification technology designed to increase precipitation by flying weather-resistant drones into winter storm clouds and releasing small amounts of silver iodide.
The particles provide surfaces around which ice crystals can form and grow before falling as rain or snow.
Rainmaker has also developed radar and validation systems intended to measure how much additional precipitation is attributable to individual seeding operations.
The company said it became the first private company to physically validate the results of cloud seeding operations earlier in 2026.
Over four months, Rainmaker recorded 82 seeding signatures that it said directly linked precipitation to individual flights.
Those events accounted for more than 145 million verified gallons of freshwater, equivalent to nearly the annual water consumption of 1,800 U.S. households, according to the company.
In August, Rainmaker said it produced 19 million gallons of water in approximately three hours near Homer, Alaska.
The Series B proceeds will support a significant expansion of Rainmaker’s research organization, which includes atmospheric scientists, radar and satellite specialists and materials scientists.
Research will focus on improving decisions around which clouds should be seeded, when operations should occur, how much seeding material should be deployed and where resulting precipitation would provide the greatest benefits for watersheds, agriculture, ecosystems and industry.
Rainmaker also plans to support research at national laboratories and fund weather modification research at U.S. universities.
The company expects its production economics to improve as deployments scale and additional drone teams operate simultaneously.
Rainmaker expects its water production costs during the November 2026 through April 2027 season to fall below many alternative sources of incremental supply, including desalination and programs that pay farmers to leave fields unplanted.
Beyond water production, Rainmaker ultimately plans to apply similar weather modification and atmospheric technologies to other agricultural challenges, including hail damage and poor soil conditions.
KEY QUOTES:
“The future of water is the future of everything. With this historic investment in weather modification technology, Rainmaker will continue to conduct frontier atmospheric research, cloud seed to end drought in the American west, and develop the tech stack that will make the earth more habitable for generations to come.”
Augustus Doricko, Founder and CEO of Rainmaker Technology

articles.title: Huntington Ingalls Receives $99.1 Million Navy Contract Modification For DDG 1002 Sea Trials
articles.snippet:
Huntington Ingalls Inc. has received a $99.1 million modification to a previously awarded U.S. Navy contract to support sea trials associated with DDG 1002.
The post Huntington Ingalls Receives $99.1 Million Navy Contract Modification For DDG 1002 Sea Trials appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Huntington Ingalls Receives $99.1 Million Navy Contract Modification For DDG 1002 Sea Trials
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 19, 2026
Huntington Ingalls Receives $99.1 Million Navy Contract Modification For DDG 1002 Sea Trials
Huntington Ingalls has received a $99.1 million modification to a previously awarded U.S. Navy contract to support sea trials associated with DDG 1002.
The $99,089,863 modification applies to contract N00024-22-C-2300 and increases the contract ceiling to incorporate the DDG 1002 Sea Trials scope. The additional work represents another phase of activity tied to the vessel as the Navy advances testing and evaluation efforts.
Approximately 95% of the work will be performed in Pascagoula, Mississippi, where Huntington Ingalls maintains major shipbuilding operations. The remaining 5% will be distributed across other locations, with each individual location accounting for less than 1% of the total work.
The Navy expects work covered by the modification to be completed by October 2028.
At the time of the award, approximately $59.3 million in shipbuilding and conversion funding will be obligated. The funding includes $28,355,651 in fiscal 2025 Shipbuilding and Conversion, Navy funds, representing approximately 48% of the amount being obligated, and $30,959,605 in fiscal 2026 Shipbuilding and Conversion, Navy funds, representing the remaining 52%.
The obligated funds will not expire at the end of the current fiscal year, allowing the Navy to apply the funding across the planned execution period for the contract work.
The modification specifically adds the DDG 1002 Sea Trials scope to the existing contract ceiling. Sea trials are a critical part of the shipbuilding and testing process, providing an opportunity to evaluate vessel performance and associated systems under operational conditions before later program milestones.
The award continues Huntington Ingalls’ work supporting U.S. Navy shipbuilding programs from its Pascagoula operations, which will account for the overwhelming majority of activity under the modification.
The Program Acquisition Executive Maritime in Washington, D.C., is the contracting activity for the award.
